key_insight: Role-prompting changed how frontier LLMs reasoned through complex medical cases, with the insurer perspective most strongly shifting decisions away from patient-preferred, physician-aligned care.
clinical_relevance: In healthcare workflows, an LLM’s assigned stakeholder role can materially alter recommendations, so human oversight and patient-centered evaluation are important before use in decision support.
method: Three frontier LLMs were tested: Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.4, and Gemini 3.1 Pro.
Models answered 25 ethically complex medical cases from physician, patient, and insurer perspectives across 3 runs each (675 total responses).
Outputs were compared with a six-physician panel and scored using a Patient-Centric Decision Index (PCDI).
evidence_signal: Across 20 cases with clear physician consensus, insurer-prompted responses reduced alignment with the physician majority by 50% for GPT-5.4, 45% for Gemini 3.1 Pro, and 10.5% for Opus 4.6.
watch_item: The study uses benchmarked case vignettes and abstracted ethical judgments, so real-world clinical performance and safety may differ from simulated prompt settings.
paper_title: Role-Prompting in Frontier Large Language Models Influences Clinical Reasoning in Complex Medical Cases
